PLAN YOUR REQUIREMENT

A useful brief.
A clearer next step.

Furniture frames, visible panels, enclosures and fabricated or machined metal components.

Decisions to make early

Choose the finish around the base material, intended environment and appearance. Specify visible faces, colour references, texture and any areas that must remain uncoated.

What to agree before work begins

Agree preparation, finish reference, masking, acceptance criteria and how finished parts should be handled and packed.

BEFORE YOU ENQUIRE

Questions,
answered.

Is a colour name enough to specify a finish?+

A physical sample or an agreed colour reference is more useful. Also specify the intended texture and gloss, because surfaces with the same colour can look different under different lighting.

Which areas may need masking?+

Identify threaded holes, electrical contact points, precision mating surfaces and other features that must remain free of coating. The masking requirements should be clear in the brief.

A CLEAR START

What to share.

Base material, operating environment, colour or finish reference and quantity.

Technical scope, material suitability, tolerances, inspection criteria, pricing and timing are confirmed after reviewing your requirements.
